items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No code was saved. The agent ran only throwaway `python3 -c` one-liners, and the reconstructed diff is empty, so there is no code left to judge for readability.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: No code was saved. The project asked for a re-runnable decrypt script plus an extraction script, but the agent left neither in /app, only inline one-liners. With no code left behind, this item cannot be graded.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No saved code to judge. The key 0x42 appears only in inline commands such as `bytes([b ^ 0x42 for b in wal_enc])`, with no explanation in code.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: The agent read the key 0x42 ('B') off the header bytes. After decrypting, it checked the magic 0x377f0682 and confirmed all 4 frame salts match. It then let SQLite replay the WAL (`sqlite3.connect` on the decrypted copy) and confirmed 11 rows. It did not run integrity_check.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: Steps [1]-[2] opened `sqlite3 /app/main.db` read-write while the WAL was still encrypted. By [3]/[4] main.db-wal was gone ('No such file'). The data came back only because a udocker container copy happened to exist, not because the agent made a backup first.
